\section[grato]{grato — grateful}

\label{lesson:PT-C499-grato}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for confidant, then the Portuguese for loyalty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: grato}
\textbf{grato} — \textquotedblleft{}grateful\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Estou muito grato pela vossa ajuda.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I am very grateful for your help.}
\end{quote}

More formal than \emph{obrigado}: \emph{estar grato por}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{grato} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{grātus} \textquotedblleft{}pleasing, thankful\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{grato}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{grato}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{grato}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for confidant, then the Portuguese for loyalty, then say \emph{grato} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does grato mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Grateful\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[a gratidão]{a gratidão — gratitude}

\label{lesson:PT-C499-gratidao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for loyalty, then the Portuguese for grateful.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a gratidão}
\textbf{a gratidão} — \textquotedblleft{}gratitude\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Mostrou a sua gratidão com um bolo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She showed her gratitude with a cake.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{grato}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gratidão} is built on \emph{grato} \textquotedblleft{}grateful\textquotedblright{} with \emph{-idão} (EtymDB); \emph{grato} comes from Latin \emph{grātus} \textquotedblleft{}thankful\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[ingrato]{ingrato — ungrateful}

\label{lesson:PT-C499-ingrato}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for grateful, then the Portuguese for gratitude.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: ingrato}
\textbf{ingrato} — \textquotedblleft{}ungrateful\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O filho ingrato nunca telefona à mãe.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The ungrateful son never phones his mother.}
\end{quote}

Of a job: thankless, \emph{um trabalho ingrato}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ingrato} comes from Latin \emph{ingrātus} \textquotedblleft{}unpleasant, ungrateful\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), the opposite of \emph{grātus}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ingrato}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ingrato}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ingrato}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for grateful, then the Portuguese for gratitude, then say \emph{ingrato} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does ingrato mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Ungrateful\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[fiel]{fiel — faithful, loyal}

\label{lesson:PT-C499-fiel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for gratitude, then the Portuguese for ungrateful.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: fiel}
\textbf{fiel} — \textquotedblleft{}faithful, loyal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O cão é um amigo fiel.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A dog is a faithful friend.}
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{fiéis}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fiel} is inherited, through Old Portuguese, from Latin \emph{fidēlis} \textquotedblleft{}faithful\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{fidēs} \textquotedblleft{}faith\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a fidelidade]{a fidelidade — faithfulness, fidelity}

\label{lesson:PT-C499-fidelidade}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for ungrateful, then the Portuguese for faithful.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a fidelidade}
\textbf{a fidelidade} — \textquotedblleft{}faithfulness, fidelity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A fidelidade é importante num casamento.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Faithfulness is important in a marriage.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Cartão de fidelidade} — a loyalty card.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fidelidade} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{fidēlitās} \textquotedblleft{}faithfulness\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{fidēlis}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a fidelidade}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for ungrateful, then the Portuguese for faithful, then say \emph{a fidelidade} again
\end{itemize}
